content.content:
# Path App

Path App is a collaborative 3D mapping and navigation project for Hack Western 13. Walk a route with a LiDAR-capable phone, turn the capture into an interactive 3D view, and send someone a link or QR code they can use to find their way.

Visitors can see what a hallway, entrance, or turn looks like before they reach it. Event teams can map rooms and booths, schools and companies can share routes across their campuses, and hikers can share trails they’ve walked. Capture can be handheld or hands-free with a custom 3D-printed wearable phone mount.

## Start here

1. **[Set up your laptop](prompts/team-chat.md)** with the copy-paste commands for your OS.
2. **[Open the live team board](https://github.com/darkprince558/path-app/issues/8)** to see who owns each task and their latest checkpoint. [Create or claim a task](docs/tasks.md) from GitHub or the terminal.
3. **[Start your agent task](prompts/start-task.md)** in its own worktree. Record reusable decisions and findings in the [team notebook](knowledge/README.md).

The [editable roadmap](planning/ROADMAP.md) shows the next milestones. The [planning index](planning/README.md) links the architecture, deployment and demo plans.

Our first milestone is to upload one real scan, share an unlisted link, and open the interactive 3D view on a second phone. Scans can be **Public** (listed for everyone), **Unlisted** (anyone with the link), or **Private** (owner and invited accounts).

| Building | Start with |
| --- | --- |
| Website and 3D viewer | [Arielle’s web workspace](apps/web/README.md) |
| Uploads, sharing and access | [Sam’s API workspace and local commands](services/api/README.md) · [Live deployment plan](docs/deployment.md) |
| Phone capture and export | [Krishna and Anish’s capture workspace](apps/capture/README.md) |
| Shared decisions and development rules | [Architecture](docs/architecture.md) · [Human and coding-agent workflow](AGENTS.md) |
| Working in Claude Code and Codex | [Set up Entire](docs/entire.md) · [Claim a task and launch parallel agents](docs/agent-tasks.md) · [Handoff and review skills](docs/agent-skills.md) |

Run `make check` from the repo root with Python 3.9+ and Make. This checks a synthetic venue and exercises the local upload/share API, including grants and revocation. Start the mock with `make dev-api`. It stores scans for the current process and serves a download page for integration. The guest 3D website, durable backend and device capture are the team's implementation work.

## Hackathon MVP

1. **Capture** a small venue section with a phone’s camera and LiDAR.
2. **Map** the scan into a viewable 3D scene using camera-colored point clouds. Map owners connect walkable waypoints, label destinations, and align contributed sections using manually verified anchors.
3. **Publish** the map and scene assets in the cloud. Map owners approve contributed scans, then share the map via a link or QR code.
4. **Navigate** from a QR-marked starting point to a selected destination. The browser computes a route on the waypoint graph with A* or Dijkstra and draws it over the 3D scene.

Gemini will analyze scan images and return structured suggestions for room numbers, signs, entrances, stairs, and landmarks, along with draft directions. Map owners review suggestions before publishing.

The demo target is one real venue section, two destinations, one route opened from a QR code, and one approved contributed scan appearing in the guest view.

## Team

- **Sam** — Backend APIs, data model, cloud storage, uploads, and event sharing.
- **Krishna and Anish** — Phone capture, scan processing, alignment, and upload integration.
- **Arielle** — Frontend, 3D viewer, route editing, pathfinding, and event experience.

## Prize strategy

Build one demo for **Best Use of Gemini API** and **Most Adventurous**. A first-time visitor chooses an unfamiliar destination, opens a scan and follows a landmark cue grounded in the actual capture. See the [ranked prize plan and 90-second demo](docs/prize-plan.md) and the [Gemini landmark design](docs/gemini-demo.md).

# Website

Arielle owns the website: the signed-in home, upload and sharing, and the guest 3D viewer. Build the website here. Start with an upload control, the three visibility choices, a copy-link action and a guest route at `/s/<shareId>`. Display upload, loading and processing failures where they occur.

## Authentication

The existing Next.js backend owns Auth0. React uses `AuthProvider` / `useAuth` and `/api/users/me`, with full-page Sign in / Sign out links. My maps and owner pages require a verified session; Community and authorized guest views work signed out. API requests use same-origin cookies and clear account state on 401. No frontend SDK, tokens or secrets are needed. Run `npm run test:auth:browser` for synthetic browser coverage. See the [production setup and real-login checklist](../../docs/auth0-production.md).

## Automatic routes from approved scans

The existing space and shared-GLB viewers now have **Automatic route** and
**Show NavMesh debug** controls. Verify calibrated metre alignment, enable automatic
routing, then double-click two floor points. Manual graph and saved routes remain
available when the mode is off. See the [full workflow and synthetic tests](../../docs/scan-automatic-routing.md).

Yes, this is possible, and it only needs changes inside the viewer (`apps/web/src/components/SpaceViewer.tsx` and `apps/web/src/lib/scan-surfaces.ts`). I haven't changed anything yet: no branch, no edits. One thing needs your decision first (below).

## What I learned

- **The app:** someone walks a hallway with an iPhone's LiDAR. The capture is fused into a GLB and uploaded through your Next.js API. Guests open it at `/spaces/:id` or `/s/:shareId` in `SpaceViewer` (React Three Fiber). The same three.js objects are used for display, for double-click picking and for building the Recast NavMesh that automatic routing uses.
- **What the scans are:** I opened `paths/Walk 2134 - 34 sections/Hallway.glb`. It's one mesh of 1.37M triangles from "Path Capture depth fusion", with a colour and a normal per vertex. It has no texture, no ARKit surface labels, and a plain material that ignores metal and reflection. The other two walks in `paths/` look similar.
- **Antialiasing is already on.** The viewer sets `antialias: true` with a DPR of 1–2. So the roughness probably isn't jagged edges. A raw depth-fusion mesh tends to look rough because:
  1. **Noisy normals:** small bumps in the fused surface catch the lights, so flat walls and floors look lumpy. This is likely the biggest cause.
  2. **Blotchy colour:** one camera colour per vertex at voxel spacing gives speckle and seams where sections meet.
  3. **Flat depth:** there's no ambient occlusion, so corners and the edges of furniture don't stand out.
  4. **Thin geometry shimmers** while orbiting, which built-in antialiasing doesn't fully fix.
- **The key constraint:** routing, picking and the NavMesh all read this geometry. Every fix should only change how the mesh is drawn, never where its vertices are. That's how `scan-surfaces.ts` already works, and it keeps this task separate from the pathing fix that comes next.

## Proposed approach (viewer only)

1. **Smooth the normals, not the positions:** average each vertex's normal over its neighbours. Walls and floors shade smoothly, and the geometry doesn't change.
2. **Lightly smooth vertex colours** over the same neighbours to reduce speckle.
3. **Add screen-space ambient occlusion and SMAA** through `@react-three/postprocessing`. On phones these would be capped or switched off.
4. **Keep it inside `ScanLook` / `prepareScanSurfaces`.** Steps 1 and 2 run once at load, steps 3–4 are render effects, and there are unit tests plus before/after screenshots.

## The decision I need

**Arielle's open PR #57 (`feature/scan-look-2`) changes the same files.** It changes the lights and tone curve in `SpaceViewer.tsx`, and it hides ceilings using the vertex normals (`normal.y < -0.5`). If I smooth normals on `main`, we'd conflict, and I could change which faces her code treats as ceiling. My suggestion: either wait for #57 to merge, or build on top of her branch and add her as a reviewer, as `AGENTS.md` asks when a shared area changes. Which do you want?

## Other things that would help

- **What "rough" looks like to you:** a screenshot, or a word like lumpy surfaces, speckled colour, jagged edges, holes or floating bits. If you don't have one, I can start the viewer locally, load `Hallway.glb` from `paths/`, and take my own before/after screenshots.
- **Performance target:** which phones the demo has to stay smooth on. Ambient occlusion on 1.37M triangles costs real GPU time, so I'd keep it off on phones unless you say otherwise.
- **Confirming the data stays local:** I'll use the `paths/` walks only to test. They contain real camera frames, so they stay out of commits, PRs and prompts.

I'll do this myself rather than split it across subagents, since it's one focused change.

import json,struct,numpy as np
p="/home/sam/Downloads/2026-11-21 2333 - 3D map.glb"
b=open(p,'rb').read()
n=struct.unpack('<I',b[12:16])[0]
d=json.loads(b[20:20+n]); bin0=20+n+8
print(d['asset'], d.get('extensionsUsed'), 'nodes',d['nodes'])
pr=d['meshes'][0]['primitives'][0]; print(pr['attributes'], len(d['meshes']))
def acc(i):
  a=d['accessors'][i]; bv=d['bufferViews'][a['bufferView']]
  dt={5126:np.float32,5125:np.uint32,5123:np.uint16,5121:np.uint8}[a['componentType']]
  k={'SCALAR':1,'VEC3':3,'VEC4':4}[a['type']]
  off=bin0+bv.get('byteOffset',0)+a.get('byteOffset',0)
  return np.frombuffer(b,dt,a['count']*k,off).reshape(-1,k) if k>1 else np.frombuffer(b,dt,a['count'],off)
P=acc(pr['attributes']['POSITION']); I=acc(pr['indices']).reshape(-1,3)
print('verts',len(P),'tris',len(I)); print('min',P.min(0),'max',P.max(0))
a,bb,c=P[I[:,0]],P[I[:,1]],P[I[:,2]]; N=np.cross(bb-a,c-a); A=np.linalg.norm(N,axis=1)/2
Nn=N/np.maximum(2*A[:,None],1e-12)
for ax,name in enumerate('xyz'):
  up=A[Nn[:,ax]>0.77].sum(); dn=A[Nn[:,ax]<-0.77].sum(); print(f'{name}: +facing area {up:.1f} m2, -facing {dn:.1f} m2')
print('total area',A.sum())
# floor height histogram for upward faces
cy=(a[:,1]+bb[:,1]+c[:,1])/3; m=Nn[:,1]>0.77
h,e=np.histogram(cy[m],bins=20,weights=A[m]); print([ (round(e[i],2),round(h[i],1)) for i in range(20)])
if 'NORMAL' in pr['attributes']:
  VN=acc(pr['attributes']['NORMAL']); fn=VN[I].mean(1); agree=(np.sum(fn*Nn,1)>0).mean(); print('winding agrees with vertex normals:',agree)
EOF
